item.title: China: the indispensable partner of Maduro’s Venezuela
item.description: China was the dominant buyer of Venezuelan oil under deposed president Nicolas Maduro, the fulcrum of a symbiotic partnership that propped up the South American economy and gave Beijing regional influence. item.title: Tai Po fire: Gov’t proposes 9 rehousing plans; on-site redevelopment of Wang Fuk Court may take a decade
item.description: The Hong Kong government has proposed nine rehousing plans for homeowners of Tai Po’s fire-hit Wang Fuk Court, ranging from an option allowing relocation as early as September to an on-site redevelopment that may take a decade. item.title: Chinese University of Hong Kong’s United College Student Union disbands
item.description: A college student union at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) has disbanded, following a string of suspensions of three other college unions last month. item.title: Slow-motion justice: Not just for political cases nor only a problem for defendants
item.description: Long delays in bringing criminal cases to court have been an unlovely feature of the Hong Kong legal system for a long time. item.description: China is moving against the cyberscam tycoons making fortunes in Southeast Asia, driven by mounting public pressure and Beijing’s desire to keep control of judicial processes, analysts say. item.title: Taiwan becomes ‘super-aged society’ in 2025, gov’t data shows
item.description: Taiwan has become a “super-aged society” for the first time, with 20 percent of its shrinking population aged 65 or older in 2025, government data showed on Friday.
